title: Pilobol.us P3-09: import the 21 Git items into the production CMS and prove export build == live site
description:
## Goal
Import the real Pilobol.us Git content into the PRODUCTION CMS backend (21 items, 13 images) and prove, offline, that a reader build from the stored data is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the live Git-built site. The reader app and the live site are not changed.

## Context (FACT)
- Same numbers as the rehearsal ticket (measured 2026-10-06 offline): created 21 (18 published, 3 drafts), 13 images 3,096,881 bytes, 56 reader-owned assets not imported, 0 aliases, export 18 items / 12 media / 0 redirects, rebuilt site 94 files identical to live.
- Source must be git archive of origin/main web/content (tracked files only): never the local checkout (it has the two generated listing pages and a wip branch).
- Media goes to the production media bucket under media/assets/<slug>/..., private bucket, guest-readable via the Storage rules (media/*); S3MediaStore stores sha256 in object metadata so re-runs do not re-upload.
- The CMS backend must already hold the Phase 2 schema (the production CMS ticket) and the admin user exists.
- Draft items (3) are already public in the Git repo; in the CMS they become private drafts.

## Exact steps
1. Scratch as in the rehearsal ticket (clone, git archive, venv with the SAME pinned papyrus-newsroom as production runs, e.g. 1.0.0.dev<N>). Generate outputs for production: npx ampx generate outputs --app-id d11eu9hbs2mipk --branch main --out-dir scratch/prod (read-only; contains public ids only).
2. Ryan yes: mint the JWT for the production backend (papyrus auth refresh-jwt --write-env scratch/.env; reads SSM /amplify/d11eu9hbs2mipk/main-branch-<hash>/PAPYRUS_JWT_SECRET; never print it; delete scratch/.env afterwards).
3. Dry run: papyrus content import-markus --content-dir scratch/src/web/content --draft-dirs drafts=articles --dry-run --json. Review with Ryan: expected counts above. Stop on any difference.
4. Ryan yes (LIVE): the same command with --apply --bucket <production media bucket from the outputs>. No --rebuild-app-id (the reader still builds from Git; a rebuild would be a no-op anyway). Re-run: created 0, updated 0, mediaUnchanged 13.
5. Verify (read-only): scan COUNT Item 21, PublishedItem 18, MediaAsset 13 (and PublishedMediaAsset 12) on the production tables; aws s3 ls of media/ = 13 objects; aws s3api get-bucket-policy-status shows IsPublic false.
6. Export and rebuild offline: papyrus content export-published --out scratch/export --clean (expect 18/12/0), assemble with the Git reader-owned assets (no-clobber overlay), build in scratch, then verify-parity.py: (a) --a scratch Git build --b scratch CMS build: identical; (b) --dist ... --live https://pilobol.us --narration: 94/94 and 11/11.
7. Slugs and URLs: confirm every exported path equals its Git path (diff of file lists), _papyrus/redirects.json is empty and the live site has no redirects to carry over.

## Acceptance checks
- Counts and idempotence as above; export + build == live (94/94, 11/11).
- Drafts are not in PublishedItem and not in the export without --drafts.

## Rollback
Re-importing is idempotent and never deletes. To undo the import: delete the 21 Items, their MediaAsset rows and the 13 objects (data deletion: Ryan only, explicit yes; or leave them unpublished with papyrus content unpublish). The live site never reads them yet, so leaving them is harmless.

## Risks
- Content edited in the CMS later is not overwritten by a re-import (skippedEditedInCms): do not edit before the parity proof.
- Importing from the wrong tree (generated listing pages) would add two junk page items (counts 23): the expected numbers catch it.

## Needs Ryan
Yes for the JWT mint (step 2) and the apply (step 4).

## Common rules (apply to every Phase 3 Pilobol.us ticket)
- Plan: docs/migrations/pilobol-us.md (AnthusAI/Papyrus, PR from branch docs/PPY-3367d3-pilobol-us-migration-plan). Facts there were verified 2026-10-06; marked FACT or ASSUMPTION. Re-verify anything you depend on before acting.
- LIVE steps (marked LIVE) touch production resources (apps d1od6t7lzbwanr and d11eu9hbs2mipk, their branches, domains, stack amplify-app-shell-pilobol-us, the CMS backend). Do them ONLY after Ryan's explicit yes in chat for that step. Everything else is read-only AWS (list/get/describe) or scratch work.
- Read AGENTS.local.md first. AWS_PROFILE=legacy, region us-east-1 (SSO login is Ryan's). Never print an env var or secret VALUE (names only; the apps hold secrets in env vars and SSM). Never run ampx pipeline-deploy locally (Amplify builds do that).
- The local checkout /Users/home/Projects/Pilobol.us is read-only for us, and its build REWRITES content front matter and generated files: never build there. Build only in scratch copies of a fresh clone (git clone https://github.com/AnthusAI/Pilobol.us, or git archive origin/main).
- Papyrus repo work: worktree of origin/develop under /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus-worktrees/, branch feature/PPY-<id>-<slug> (or chore/ for docs), PR into develop, never merge to main, never git stash, conventional commits, commit trailer Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>, PR body ends with the Claude Code generated-with line. Pilobol.us repo work: a feature branch and a PR; never push or merge to its main (production reader deploys from main). In /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus run only kbs; never git add or commit there. Tickets live on the PPY board; do not use kbs in the Pilobol.us repo (PILO board is stories only).
- Keep article text byte-identical everywhere. Narration (Auritus) hashes cover article text: any text change re-queues Batch jobs.
- Update this ticket with branch, PR link, command output and numbers when done.
right_now_summary: The 21 Git items and 13 images await production import and offline parity checks against the live site.
